blocker.summary: The r399 allocator double-issue is RESOLVED (r413/r414/r415). r416/r417 established boot now progresses past sub_821D5F48 and the per-frame loop runs sustained. r418/r419/r420 found and root-caused (from source alone) a real, standalone-reproducible shutdown hang on the r414-fixed binary: NativeRuntime::shutdown() calls native_guest_threads_stop_and_join(), which does an unconditional, timeout-less thread.join() on every ExCreateThread-spawned worker; this only completes if every such thread happens to be parked in a generated wait-stub (r277's clean-shutdown mechanism) at the moment shutdown is requested. r421 pinned this live: worked around this sandbox's ptrace_scope restriction (which blocks attaching to an already-running process) by having gdb itself LAUNCH the binary via `run` -- that is never subject to the restriction. Interrupted the process mid-hang and captured every thread's backtrace. Main thread is exactly where r420 predicted (stop_and_join -> thread.join -> shutdown -> main). The specific worker thread it blocks on (an ExCreateThread worker, 10 nested PPC call frames of real game logic, sub_821F8008<-...<-sub_823A8F90) is stuck acquiring g_dpc_level_mutex inside the __imp__KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel host stub -- not parked in any wait-stub at all. That mutex (tools/materialize_native_import_stubs.py:186, a documented r191 design choice, not new) is a single std::recursive_mutex shared across ALL guest threads to emulate the single-core Xbox 360 semantic that raising IRQL alone prevents preemption -- a reasoned choice, since this project runs guest code on real concurrent host threads. But KeRaiseIrqlToDpcLevel/KfLowerIrql are two separately-generated PPC functions (materialize_native_import_stubs.py:904-912), so the lock()/unlock() pair is necessarily raw, not RAII-guarded (no std::lock_guard is architecturally possible across two independent generated function bodies). If a GuestThreadTerminated exception (r277/r417's own clean-shutdown mechanism) is thrown on a thread between its Raise and matching Lower -- e.g. it raised IRQL then entered a wait -- stack unwinding skips the unlock() and permanently orphans the global mutex, hanging every other thread (and thus shutdown()'s own join loop) forever. This is not confirmed by directly observing the orphaning moment (the thread that leaked the lock had already exited by the time of capture), but is consistent with every fact gathered r418-r421 and explains why this was never seen before r414 (boot never previously ran enough concurrent real game logic for this window to be hit). Named for r422: design and live-verify a fix (either make IRQL state genuinely thread_local, matching real hardware and eliminating the bug class, or add an exception-safety guard that releases any residual raised IRQL along a thread's GuestThreadTerminated path) -- this is a design decision, not applied unilaterally this cycle. Verify any fix with a standalone (non-gdb) launch, per r419's methodology lesson. The standing uncommitted-tree situation (r239+, over the 2026-09-02 mass deletion) remains the user's decision, untouched -- reports and named tool scripts for r413-r421 were committed individually, the broader tree state was not.
